text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.59% today to $141.73, continuing a sharp two-week climb of 13.25%. The move reflects escalating Middle East tensions: Iran threatened strikes on U.S. warships, Saudi Aramco facilities came under attack, and the International Energy Agency warned of tightening oil supplies—all pushing crude prices higher. With U.S. oil at $96.24 per barrel (up substantially from earlier in the month), refiners and oil producers benefit directly from higher commodity prices and the prospect of sustained demand for fuel.

The broader picture is a supply crunch expected to stretch into 2027, driven by Iran-related disruptions, falling diesel inventories, and persistent demand. That structural tightness—not just today's headlines, but the IEA's forward guidance on constrained markets—is what's fueling the stock's two-week rally, giving the company visibility into sustained higher energy prices over a longer horizon.
